[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Debugging Out of Memory (OOM) Errors in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Out of Memory (OOM) errors are among the most common and frustrating issues encountered when running distributed workloads in Apache Spark. They typically manifest as java.lang.OutOfMemoryError or container killed by YARN/Kubernetes due to memory exhaustion."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Spark Memory Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into debugging, it is crucial to understand how Spark divides its executor memory. The total executor memory (configured via spark.executor.memory) is split primarily into Reserved Memory, Spark Memory (Execution and Storage), and User Memory."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Execution Memory: Used for shuffles, joins, sorts, and aggregations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Storage Memory: Used for caching datasets and broadcast variables."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"User Memory: Used for user-defined data structures and UDFs."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Causes of OOM Errors"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"OOM errors generally occur on either the Driver or the Executor nodes, driven by specific anti-patterns in data processing."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Driver OOM: Collecting massive datasets to the driver using collect() or broadcast joins with extremely large tables."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Executor OOM (Data Skew): Uneven distribution of data causing a single task to process more partitions than its memory can handle."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Executor OOM (GC Overhead): Too many small objects filling the JVM heap, leading to frequent Garbage Collection pauses."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Strategy"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"When an OOM error occurs, follow this systematic approach to identify and resolve the root cause."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Check the Spark UI. Look at the stages and tasks tab to see if a specific task failed or if certain tasks took significantly longer or processed much more data than others."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Identify Driver vs Executor. Check if the error log mentions the driver JVM or an executor container being terminated."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Mitigation and Code Best Practices"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apply the following configurations and code modifications to prevent OOM errors."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2000")
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Avoid using collect() on large dataframes. Instead, write results to disk or use take(n) for inspection."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Bad practice for large datasets
# data = df.collect()

# Good practice
df.show(10)"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Data Skew"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"If data skew is causing executor OOM during joins or groupBy operations, consider salting your keys to distribute the workload evenly across partitions."}]
